key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines thermal welding simulation, AI surrogates, and robot control to screen in-space joining strategies before experimental testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support adaptive welding control when robot travel speed changes, helping maintain weld geometry during complex seam traversal.
method: Finite-volume thermal model with phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates evaluated using repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated UR5 welding with proportional power-setting control along an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; 74/80 held-out solver responses fell within nominal 90% predictive intervals, and finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative weld-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-only; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation are still needed.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
